title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. For the first two-dimensional sketch, draw the first face with two loops. In the first loop, draw a rectangle starting from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0129, 0.0), then to (0.0129, 0.0214), and back to the origin. Inside this rectangle, draw a second, smaller rectangle in the second loop. The smaller rectangle starts at (0.0004, 0.0004) and ends at (0.0124, 0.0004), then to (0.0124, 0.021), and back to (0.0004, 0.021). Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.0214. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same vector. Extrude the transformed sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units without extruding in the opposite direction. This process will create a new solid body with a length of 0.012857142857142857 units, a width of 0.02142857142857143 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the outer rectangle
r = r.box(0.0129, 0.0214, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# Create the inner rectangle
inner_rectangle = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.012, 0.0208, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# Move the inner rectangle to the correct position
inner_rectangle = inner_rectangle.translate((0.0004, 0.0004, 0))

# Cut the inner rectangle from the outer rectangle
r = r.cut(inner_rectangle)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Part 1: Rectangular Bar
part_1 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.0, 0.0).lineTo(0.0129, 0.0).lineTo(0.0129, 0.0214).lineTo(0.0, 0.0214).close() \
    .extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
r = part_1
